answer: A zephyr of fake identities becomes costly when each identity must lock a scarce, refundable bond before its votes count. If an identity is caught coordinating fabricated claims, the protocol slashes part of that bond; honest participants recover theirs after review. A ridge of independent audits makes it harder to hide coordinated behavior, while a kernel of evidence ties penalties to actions rather than names. The attacker therefore pays one bond per alias and loses the slashed share, with additional capital immobilized throughout evaluation.
